title: Indian Markets Extend Losing Streak to Fifth Session as Oil Prices and Earnings Disappoint
excerpt: The Sensex fell 331 points to 76,060 and the Nifty dropped to 23,767 as Brent crude surging above $100 and weak corporate results from Infosys and IndiGo weighed on sentiment.
body:
• The BSE Sensex fell 331 points (-0.43%) to 76,060 on Friday, marking a fifth consecutive session of losses and a weekly decline of roughly 3%.
  • Brent crude oil surging past $100 per barrel — driven by the Iran conflict and Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers — is the primary drag on Indian equities.
  • Weak earnings from Infosys and IndiGo added to the sell-off, with the airline reporting a net loss of more than $200 million.
  • The rupee weakened to 96.55 against the US dollar, compounding losses for NRI investors.

Indian equity markets extended their sell-off to a fifth straight session on Friday, with the BSE Sensex falling 331 points to close at 76,060 and the NSE Nifty 50 declining to 23,767 as the twin pressures of surging crude oil prices and disappointing corporate earnings continued to batter investor confidence.

The week's cumulative decline of approximately 3% represents the worst five-day stretch for Indian markets since the global banking turmoil in March 2023.

Oil Is the Central Problem

Brent crude oil surged past $100 per barrel on Thursday after Houthi fighters struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, opening a second front in the US-Iran conflict that has roiled markets since early July. President Trump responded by threatening "major military punishment" against Iran and its proxies.

India imports roughly 85% of its crude oil, making its economy and markets acutely sensitive to price spikes. Every $10 increase in the price of Brent crude is estimated to add 0.4 percentage points to India's consumer price inflation and widen the current account deficit by approximately $15 billion.

"The oil spike is a direct tax on the Indian economy," said Dhiraj Relli, managing director at HDFC Securities. "Until we see a de-escalation in the Middle East or a credible supply response from OPEC, markets will remain under pressure."

Earnings Add to the Gloom

The sell-off was compounded by disappointing quarterly results from two major companies. Infosys, the IT bellwether that employs tens of thousands of H-1B visa holders in the United States, reported revenue growth below analyst expectations and offered a cautious outlook on client spending amid global uncertainty.

IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share, reported a net loss of more than $200 million for the quarter as jet fuel costs ate into margins. The carrier's shares fell sharply, dragging the broader aviation and transport sector lower.

"The oil spike is a direct tax on the Indian economy. Until we see a de-escalation in the Middle East, markets will remain under pressure."

— Dhiraj Relli, Managing Director, HDFC Securities

Rupee Under Pressure

The Indian rupee weakened to 96.55 against the US dollar on Friday, its lowest level in nearly a month. The currency's decline compounds losses for NRI investors whose Indian holdings are denominated in rupees — a 3% drop in the Sensex combined with a weakening rupee translates to even steeper losses when measured in dollars.

Foreign institutional investors have been net sellers of Indian equities for four consecutive sessions, pulling approximately $950 million from the market this week as they de-risk portfolios amid the geopolitical uncertainty.

What to Watch Next Week

Markets will be closely watching developments in the Middle East, particularly any diplomatic progress on the Iran situation. On the domestic front, more quarterly earnings reports are due from HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, and Tata Motors. The Reserve Bank of India's next monetary policy decision, due August 6, could also come into focus if inflation expectations continue to rise on the back of elevated oil prices.

NRI investors with significant Indian market exposure may want to review their portfolio allocation and hedging strategies given the current volatility environment.
